facts.verified: aem-cli 16.22.16 src/content/{clone,add,commit,push}.cmd.js exist; src/content/da-auth.js stores the DA token in .hlx/.da-token.json (CLI-managed login). 'push does not preview' taken from goals.md, not verified

facts.claim: `aem up` serves files from the project's ./content/ folder first and proxies to the preview origin only for files not found there.
facts.verified: aem-cli 16.22.16 src/server/HelixServer.js:L475-477 ('Check content/ first — prefer local content checkout over proxy'); src/server/BaseServer.js:L161-164 logs 'Serving content from local content/, proxying missing files from ...'; CONTENT_DIR='content' (src/content/content-shared.js)
facts.question: When the AEM CLI dev server runs, where does it look for page content first, and when does it fall back to the remote origin?

facts.claim: Test content lives on the block library page `/docs/library/blocks/<block>`; use `/drafts` for stress/edge cases or projects without a library. For non-DA sources, hand-written HTML in ./content/ is for local testing only.
facts.source: SKILL.md:43 (prerequisite 'Test content exists (in CMS or local drafts)')
facts.verified: goals.md (project convention; not a platform rule)

facts.claim: In a git worktree, `aem up` picks a branch-derived port (3000-3999) and logs it; use the port aem up logs instead of assuming localhost:3000.
facts.verified: aem-cli 16.22.16 src/up.cmd.js:L105-112 ('Git worktree detected. Using port … for branch …'); src/git-utils.js:L406 hashBranchToPort(branch, 3000, 1000); src/up.js:L53 defaultDescription '3000 (branch-derived in Git worktrees)'
facts.question: Running `aem up` inside a git worktree, which port does the dev server listen on and how do you find it?

facts.claim: Header and footer blocks are rendered into <header>/<footer>, outside <main>, so `main .{block}` selectors cannot style them; boilerplate styles them with `header …`/`footer …` selectors.
facts.verified: aem-boilerplate@5cea543 scripts/aem.js:L599-626 loadHeader/loadFooter build the block inside body > header / body > footer; blocks/header/header.css and blocks/footer/footer.css selectors start with `header`/`footer`
facts.question: Where in the page DOM do EDS header and footer blocks end up, and what does that mean for how their CSS can be scoped?

facts.claim: Block CSS may also target the block's platform-added wrapper or containing section when needed (e.g. `.hero-container .hero-wrapper`).
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/developer/markup-sections-blocks 'In certain cases it makes sense to use the block's wrapper or containing section for the selector as well.'; aem-boilerplate@5cea543 blocks/hero/hero.css:L1-4
facts.question: Besides the block's own class, what platform-added elements can a block's stylesheet legitimately target, and how are they named?

facts.claim: Follow the project's existing scoping convention for block CSS (check existing blocks); boilerplate and block-collection blocks use bare `.{block}` prefixes.
facts.verified: aem-boilerplate@5cea543 blocks/cards/cards.css, columns.css, hero.css; aem-block-collection@a8ffc6c blocks/*/*.css (no `main .` prefixes)

facts.claim: Prefixing with `main` adds an element selector to specificity, which matters when competing with global `main …` rules in styles.css.
facts.verified: CSS specificity: `main .x` = (0,1,1) vs `.x` = (0,1,0); aem-boilerplate@5cea543 styles/styles.css has `main img` (L281), `main > .section > div` (L303)

facts.claim: Choose how to load a third-party script by context — via loadDelayed() (consent-check.js/consented.js or delayed.js), an IntersectionObserver, on user interaction, or a timed loader — rather than putting everything in the delayed phase.
facts.skillSays: delayed.js listed as the home for 'Marketing, analytics, third-party integrations' (SKILL.md:248)
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/docs/dev-collab-and-good-practices ('Add the dependencies where needed via loadScript() to the specific block ... consider using an IntersectionObserver'); https://www.aem.live/docs/faq ('load scripts only when needed using loadScript() within specific blocks or IntersectionObserver to defer execution'); aem-block-collection@a8ffc6c blocks/embed/embed.js:L90-112 (click on placeholder or IntersectionObserver); https://www.aem.live/developer/keeping-it-100 (delayed phase timing)
facts.question: What options exist for loading a third-party script in an EDS project, and how do you decide between them?

facts.claim: Scripts that need user consent (analytics, martech, tag managers) belong in consented.js, which consent-check.js imports only once consent is granted; consent-check.js is where a real CMP (OneTrust, Cookiebot) is wired in.
facts.verified: aem-boilerplate@5cea543 scripts/consented.js ('add functionality that requires user consent here (analytics, martech, etc.)'), scripts/consent-check.js; https://www.aem.live/developer/cmp-integration
facts.question: In current boilerplate, where do analytics and martech scripts that require user consent go, and what triggers their loading?

facts.claim: The boilerplate's dummy consent check declines by default; append `?consent=accept` to a URL to exercise the consented path locally.
facts.verified: aem-boilerplate@5cea543 scripts/consent-check.js hasConsent() (query param accept/true/1/yes; default false); https://www.aem.live/developer/cmp-integration
facts.question: With the boilerplate's default consent implementation, will consent-gated scripts load, and how can you test that path locally?

facts.claim: The delayed phase should start no earlier than ~3 seconds after LCP, but current boilerplate loadDelayed() has no timer; if a minimum delay is needed, add it explicitly (a timed loader).
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/developer/keeping-it-100 ('the delayed phase should still not start until at least three seconds after the LCP event ... the boilerplate's loadDelayed() no longer enforces this with a hard-coded timer, so ... add it explicitly'); aem-boilerplate@5cea543 scripts/scripts.js:L206-209
facts.question: How long after LCP should the EDS delayed phase begin, and does the current boilerplate enforce that delay?

facts.claim: A third-party library needed by only one block should be loaded from that block (e.g. with loadScript()), not added to head.html; head.html must stay free of martech/third-party scripts.
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/docs/dev-collab-and-good-practices ('Don't add 3rd party libraries to your <head> via head.html ... Add the dependencies where needed via loadScript() to the specific block'; '<head> ... should remain minimal and free of marketing technology')
facts.question: A block depends on an external JavaScript library. Where and how should that library be loaded in an EDS project?

facts.claim: Large third-party libraries or embeds in a block can be loaded only when the block scrolls into view, using an IntersectionObserver (as the block-collection embed and video blocks do).
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/docs/dev-collab-and-good-practices ('consider using an IntersectionObserver to make sure you only load them when the block depending on it is actually being scrolled into view'); aem-block-collection@a8ffc6c blocks/embed/embed.js:L105-111, blocks/video/video.js:L160-169
facts.question: How can an EDS block avoid loading a heavy third-party embed until the visitor actually reaches it?

facts.claim: Third-party embeds can be loaded on user interaction: show a placeholder (e.g. an authored image with a play button) and load the embed on click.
facts.verified: aem-block-collection@a8ffc6c blocks/embed/embed.js:L90-103 (placeholder picture + click -> loadEmbed), blocks/video/video.js:L131-157
facts.question: When an embed block has an authored placeholder image, how do the block-collection embed/video blocks defer loading the third-party player?

facts.claim: Avoid loading from or connecting to a second origin before LCP; keep the pre-LCP payload small (rule of thumb under 100 KB).
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/developer/keeping-it-100 ('Loading from or connecting to a second origin before the LCP occurred is strongly discouraged'; 'keep the aggregate payload before the LCP is displayed below 100kb')
facts.question: What network constraints should code that runs before LCP respect on an EDS site?

facts.claim: Third-party code that must change above-the-fold content (e.g. Adobe Target personalization) is loaded in the eager phase, awaited before the first section loads, rather than delayed.
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/developer/target-integration (edit loadEager to 'await alloyLoadedPromise' before loadSection(main.querySelector('.section'), waitForFirstImage)); https://www.aem.live/developer/martech-integration ('enable personalization early in the page load')
facts.question: If a third-party tool personalizes the hero content of a page, in which loading phase does it need to run, and why?

facts.claim: Once a third-party script's blocking time is removed (or moved to a web worker), it can be loaded in the lazy phase instead of delayed.
facts.verified: https://www.aem.live/developer/keeping-it-100 ('Once the problems are fixed, those libraries can easily be added to the lazy phase and be loaded earlier')
facts.question: Under what condition can a third-party script be moved out of the EDS delayed phase into an earlier phase?

facts.claim: Blocks within a section load one after another (each loadBlock is awaited in order), and sections load one after another.
facts.verified: aem-boilerplate@5cea543 scripts/aem.js:L650-662 loadSection (await loadBlock in a for loop), L670-679 loadSections (await loadSection in a for loop)
facts.question: Within an EDS page, are block modules loaded in parallel or in sequence, and how does that affect a slow block's neighbours?

facts.claim: The LCP candidate is the first in the first section; it is found after all of that section's blocks have decorated, then set to loading=eager and awaited — so a block that builds or swaps the hero image must have it in the DOM when decorate resolves.
facts.verified: aem-boilerplate@5cea543 scripts/aem.js:L632-645 waitForFirstImage(section.querySelector('img')), called by loadSection after the block loop (L656-659); https://www.aem.live/developer/keeping-it-100 ('wait with guessing the LCP candidate ... until the first block has made the necessary changes to the DOM')
facts.question: How does the boilerplate determine which image is the LCP candidate, and at what point in loading is it chosen?

facts.claim: Sections are hidden (display:none) until they finish loading, and the body is hidden until the `appear` class is added.
facts.verified: aem-boilerplate@5cea543 scripts/aem.js:L496 decorateSections sets section.style.display='none', L661 loadSection clears it; styles/styles.css:L73-85 body {display:none}, body.appear {display:block}; scripts/scripts.js:L168
facts.question: What is the visibility of an EDS section before its blocks have loaded, and when does it become visible?

facts.claim: data-block-status moves initialized -> loading -> loaded; it becomes `loaded` only after the block CSS has loaded and decorate() has resolved, so code/tests waiting for a block should wait for `data-block-status="loaded"`.
facts.verified: aem-boilerplate@5cea543 scripts/aem.js:L577 (initialized), L538 (loading), L558-563 (Promise.all([cssLoaded, decorationComplete]) then 'loaded'); sections use data-section-status the same way (L495, L653, L660)
facts.question: How can code or a test tell that an EDS block has finished loading its CSS and running its decoration?

facts.claim: Work a block defers outside the awaited decorate() (setTimeout, IntersectionObserver, event handlers) is not covered by data-block-status="loaded" or the first-section/LCP wait.
facts.verified: aem-boilerplate@5cea543 scripts/aem.js:L549 awaits only mod.default(block); L563 sets 'loaded' right after
facts.question: If a block's decorate function schedules rendering with setTimeout, how does that interact with the block's loaded status and the first-section wait?

facts.claim: Header and footer blocks and all sections after the first load in the lazy phase, after LCP; fonts load after LCP too.
facts.verified: aem-boilerplate@5cea543 scripts/scripts.js:L186-200 loadLazy (loadHeader, loadSections, loadFooter, lazy-styles.css, loadFonts); L174-176 fonts only eager on desktop/cached; https://www.aem.live/developer/keeping-it-100 (Header and Footer, Fonts sections)
facts.question: In which loading phase do the EDS header, footer and below-the-fold sections load?
